summary: This document is a structured research discussion (swarm ID: L3) proposing a hypothesis that senolytic + NAD precursor stacking is sub-additive on the tissue NAD metabolome after CD38 load is reduced by senescent cell clearance. It is classified as a negative/assumption-kill claim at the research-discussion risk class, with no original experimental data — it synthesizes existing literature and identifies a missing factorial experiment as the key knowledge gap.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Classification
content_blocks.content: Swarm ID: L3. Status: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative). Lane: longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Novelty: assumption-kill. Method: propose-assay. OpenLabs target: discussion (PASS_NEGATIVE — not claim). Cheap-IP: kill_cost_tier=2, time_to_refute=6 weeks, ip_class=subtract-before-add, vault_hold=no. This is a public report only; private vault skipped.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim
content_blocks.content: Senolytic + NAD precursor stacking is NOT NAD-additive on the tissue metabolome. After documented senescent ablation or SASP reduction lowers CD38, a matched precursor pulse raises tissue NAD by ≤50% of the same pulse on uncleared background (sub-additive / diminishing returns) in a pre-registered WAT or liver NAD panel. This challenges the popular longevity stack assumption that senolytics and NMN/NR are additive NAD restorers.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Aging NAD decline is CD38-gated; CD38 ecto-activity degrades NMN. SASP recruits or induces CD38+ macrophages that drain tissue NAD. Clearing senescent cells or reducing SASP decreases CD38 and partially restores NAD. Once that drain is reduced, further precursor input should hit a smaller ΔNAD ceiling than precursor on high-CD38 uncleared tissue — the opposite of 'always stack both.' Key mechanistic distinction: NAD drain is largely from macrophage CD38 induced by SASP, not CD38 on the senescent cell itself.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Senolytic + NAD precursor always restores tissue NAD additively; stacking both is strictly better than either alone on the NAD metabolome.

Baseline measured (literature-supported):
- CD38 dictates age NAD decline and degrades NMN (PMID 27304511) — LITERATURE
- SASP → CD38+ macrophages → tissue NAD↓ (PMID 33199924) — LITERATURE
- Senescent ablation / SASP↓ → CD38↓ with partial NAD rebound (PMID 33199925) — LITERATURE
- Human NR raises aged muscle NAD metabolome (PMID 31412242) — LITERATURE
- Head-to-head factorial post-senolysis vs uncleared precursor ΔNAD / diminishing returns — UNKNOWN
- ≤50% marginal-ΔNAD threshold — PREDICTION

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Supporting Literature
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 27304511 / DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2016.05.006 / PMC4911708 — Camacho-Pereira 2016: Age NAD↓ requires CD38; CD38 is major in vivo NMN-degrading activity.
2. PMID 33199924 / DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00305-3 / PMC7908681 — Covarrubias 2020: SASP → CD38+ macrophages → tissue NAD↓.
3. PMID 33199925 / DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00298-z / PMC8752031 — Chini 2020: Senescent ablation / SASP↓ → CD38↓ and partial NAD recovery; CD38 ecto-block raises NAD NMN-dependently.
4. PMID 31412242 / PMC6702140 — Elhassan 2019: Oral NR augments aged human muscle NAD metabolome without a senolysis preconditioning arm (adjacent/comparator).

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Mechanism (CD38↓ after clearance) ≠ proven combo pharmacodynamics (diminishing precursor ΔNAD) — factorial experiment is missing.
2. NAD drain is largely macrophage CD38 induced by SASP, not CD38 on the senescent cell itself.
3. Synergy reviews still push precursor + CD38-axis drugs without a shared kill assay for sub-additivity after senolysis.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay / Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: In a pre-registered aged WAT or liver panel with verified CD38↓ after senescent ablation or SASP reduction, a matched precursor pulse raises tissue NAD by >50% of the same pulse on uncleared background (additivity retained; no diminishing returns).

Ablation conditions that would remove the premise:
- Remove post-clearance CD38↓ / partial NAD rebound LITERATURE → no subtract-before-add premise
- Remove factorial order contrast → any NAD rise restates precursor LITERATURE
- Remove tissue NAD primary endpoint → CD38 alone cannot show sub-additive ΔNAD

Human input needed: Lock tissue (WAT vs liver), CD38 readout (protein vs ecto-NADase), precursor identity (NMN vs NR), and the ≤50% marginal-ΔNAD band before running the ordered combo; do not invent dosing.

content_blocks.title: TRL Assessment Context
content_blocks.content: This document represents TRL 1 (basic principles observed and reported). There are no original experiments, no animal or cell data generated by the authors, and no proprietary assay results. The claim is entirely hypothesis-driven, synthesizing published literature (4 PMIDs) to identify a gap (missing factorial experiment). The proposed assay (ordered factorial WAT/liver NAD panel with CD38 readout) would constitute TRL 2 if executed. Estimated time to refute: 6 weeks (kill_cost_tier=2).

key_findings: Central hypothesis: senolytic + NAD precursor stacking is sub-additive (≤50% marginal ΔNAD) after CD38 load is reduced by senescent cell clearance — this is a PREDICTION, not experimentally confirmed.

Key mechanistic chain supported by literature: CD38 gates age-related NAD decline (PMID 27304511); SASP induces CD38+ macrophages that drain tissue NAD (PMID 33199924); senescent ablation reduces CD38 and partially restores NAD (PMID 33199925).
Critical knowledge gap: No factorial experiment exists comparing post-senolysis precursor ΔNAD vs. precursor-alone ΔNAD on uncleared background — this is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN.
The ≤50% marginal-ΔNAD threshold is a PREDICTION with no empirical basis yet established.
Human NR raises aged muscle NAD metabolome (PMID 31412242) but without a senolysis preconditioning arm, making it an adjacent comparator only.
NAD drain mechanism is primarily macrophage CD38 induced by SASP, not CD38 on senescent cells themselves — important for assay design.
Proposed refutation assay: pre-registered aged WAT or liver NAD panel with verified CD38↓ post-senolysis, comparing matched precursor pulse vs. uncleared background; estimated 6 weeks to refute.
No original experimental data generated; document is a structured research discussion / hypothesis proposal at TRL 1.
